tex_content.html:
Proposition
[injectivity of $\exp _p$ on the star interior]

Source: petersen:page-0233 ↗ def:pet-ch5-segment-domain ↗ cor:pet-ch5-segments-are-geodesics

1. ch5:5.7.7If $x\in \exp _p(\operatorname {seg}^0(p))$, it is joined to $p$ by a unique segment; in particular $\exp _p$ is injective on $\operatorname {seg}^0(p)$.
Proof

↗ prop:pet-ch5-segment-domain-injective \sketch Concatenate any competing segment to $x=\sigma (t_0)$, $t_0<1$, with the tail of $\sigma $. The result is again minimizing, hence a geodesic by section 4. It agrees with $\sigma $ after $t_0$, so geodesic uniqueness propagates equality across the joining point. Thus the initial segments, and consequently their exponential initial vectors, coincide.

□
